h1:
Roi Et in 3 Days 2 Nights
City + Pagoda + Lake + Thung Kula
intro: Roi Et is one of those Isan provinces plenty of people drive straight through without stopping, even though a single province packs in several very different days out: a lake in the middle of town with a 360-degree view tower, a huge hilltop pagoda, a wide freshwater lake locals call the sea of Isan, and Thung Kula Ronghai, the plains that grow the best jasmine rice in the country. This is a 3 day 2 night self-drive plan, paced so it never feels rushed and still covers the city, the pagoda and the nature spots.

blocks.html: This trip is built for driving yourself, because Roi Et's sights are scattered in different directions. The city sits in the middle, Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol and Bueng Kluea lake are to the northeast (Selaphum–Nong Phok districts), and Thung Kula Ronghai is to the south (Suwannaphum–Kaset Wisai districts). So we keep day one in town to recover from the journey, run the northern route to the lake and the great pagoda on day two, and head south to Thung Kula and Prang Ku before leaving on day three. If you arrive in Roi Et by bus or plane, renting a car to drive yourself is the way to go, since public transport to the out-of-town spots is sparse and inflexible.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: The most comfortable time to visit Roi Et is late rainy season into early cool season (November–February): cooler air and green rice fields before harvest. Hot season (March–May) gets very hot and Thung Kula dries out. · Roi Et has a small airport with only a few flights a day from Bangkok, so book ahead for better fares. · Driving from Bangkok takes around 7–8 hours, which is why many people fly in and then rent a car at the airport or in town.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Roi Et city: Bueng Phlan Chai, Ho Wood 101, the Great Buddha

blocks.html: Day one stays mostly in town, with the sights either within walking distance or a few minutes' drive apart. Start at Bueng Phlan Chai lake in the city center, go up the Ho Wood 101 tower for a view over town, pay respects to the Great Buddha at Wat Burapha Phiram, then finish with street food at the evening market. If you arrive around midday, just start with lunch.

items.activity: Arrive in town, check in to a hotel near the city center close to Bueng Phlan Chai
items.note: Staying in town makes it easy to walk to dinner and head up the Ho Wood tower

items.activity: Lunch on local Isan food — try Tam Kratoey for som tam, larb and country chicken soup
items.note: Bold, proper Isan flavors; som tam runs around 50–70 THB a plate and you can order it as spicy as you like

items.activity: Stroll around Bueng Phlan Chai, the lake island in the heart of town, and pay respects at the City Pillar Shrine
items.note: Free entry, open 04:00–21:00, with flower gardens and shade — an easy, relaxed walk for photos

items.activity: Go up Ho Wood 101, a 35-storey city-view tower with a 360-degree view and a glass-floor skywalk
items.note: Entry around 50 THB with discounts for students and seniors; tickets sold on the 2nd floor roughly 10:00–18:00, and the very top holds a Buddha relic

items.activity: Pay respects to the Great Buddha (Phra Phuttha Rattana Mongkon Maha Muni) at Wat Burapha Phiram, a huge standing Buddha in the blessing pose
items.note: The image stands about 59 m tall (nearly 68 m including the base), the tallest standing blessing-pose Buddha in Thailand, right in town on Phadung Phanit Road

items.activity: Coffee break at a city cafe such as Four Lover The Baker, or another spot in the center
items.note: Roi Et has plenty of new cafes; drinks run around 60–90 THB — a good place to rest before dinner

items.activity: Dinner on street food at the evening market in town, or an Isan grill spot
items.note: The evening market has all the local bites — grilled meats, som tam, khanom jeen — at friendly prices

blocks.title: A few honest notes
blocks.html: The view from Ho Wood 101 is genuinely good, but the afternoon sun on the skywalk is strong and hot. For nicer light and less heat, go in the late afternoon near sunset and watch the city lights flicker on. · The zipline runs in set sessions (roughly 09:30–17:30); if you're interested, check the schedule on the day, since it's sometimes closed for maintenance.

blocks.text: Day 2 — northern route: Bueng Kluea, the sea of Isan + Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol

blocks.html: Today runs northeast. Leave town toward Selaphum district and stop at Bueng Kluea, a wide freshwater lake locals call the sea of Isan, then drive on up to Nong Phok district for the hilltop Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol. The two spots are in the same direction and doable in one day, but the total distance isn't short (the pagoda is about 80 km from town), so set off a bit early.

items.activity: Have breakfast, leave town and head for Selaphum district and Bueng Kluea
items.note: About 40 min–1 hour of smooth driving; fill up the tank before heading out of town

items.activity: Visit Bueng Kluea (the sea of Isan), a wide freshwater lake with a sandy beach and lakeside restaurants
items.note: Swim, paddle a boat, or sit at a lakeside spot; the morning breeze is cool and the crowds haven't arrived yet

items.activity: Leave Bueng Kluea and drive on up to Nong Phok district for Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol
items.note: About 1 hour; the last stretch climbs slightly into the hills, so take the curves carefully

items.activity: Lunch at a restaurant around the foot of the Nong Phok hills, or pack supplies to eat at the top
items.note: Food options up top are limited, so bring drinking water; the air up there is cooler than below

items.activity: Visit Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol at Wat Pha Nam Thip, a pagoda 101 m wide, long and tall on a green hilltop
items.note: Walk up through several levels inside the pagoda, with murals and a Buddha relic, and wide views over the Phu Phan range; dress modestly

items.activity: Stop at the nearby Pha Nam Yoi viewpoint, looking over the plains and ridges before heading down
items.note: Pha Nam Yoi is a cliff that seeps water year-round, which gives it its name, and the view makes for good photos

items.activity: Drive back into Roi Et city and rest
items.note: About 1.5 hours back, reaching town before evening — save your energy for the final day

items.activity: Dinner in town — try a moo kratha (Thai BBQ hotpot) or a relaxed Isan spot
items.note: There are several moo kratha places in town at friendly prices — a satisfying, good-value meal after a full day out

items.name: If you love nature and swimming
items.blurb: Give Bueng Kluea more time — swim, paddle a boat, linger at a lakeside spot, then head up to the great pagoda in the late afternoon.

items.name: If you're here for the temples
items.blurb: Go up the great pagoda in the late morning for nicer light and fewer people, then stop by Bueng Kluea on the way back in the afternoon.

items.name: If you're short on time
items.blurb: Make the great pagoda your priority, skip Bueng Kluea, and spend the leftover time on the city's cafes.

blocks.text: Day 3 — southern route: Thung Kula Ronghai + Prang Ku before leaving

blocks.html: The last day heads south to Thung Kula Ronghai, the plains once so dry that, as the story goes, even the traveling Kula merchants wept crossing them — yet today they grow the best jasmine rice in Thailand. On the way, stop at Prang Ku, an old Khmer sanctuary near the city. Tick off these two spots, then point the car home.

items.activity: Check out, leave town and stop first at Prang Ku in Thawat Buri district
items.note: Prang Ku is about 14 km from town, around 20 min along Highway 23 toward Yasothon

items.activity: See Prang Ku (Prasat Nong Ku), an ancient Khmer sanctuary, a hospital chapel from the reign of Jayavarman VII
items.note: A small, shady laterite sanctuary; about 30–40 min to walk around, free entry, and good for photos

items.activity: Drive south toward Suwannaphum–Kaset Wisai districts, into the Thung Kula Ronghai area
items.note: About 1–1.5 hours, with wide rice fields stretching to the horizon on both sides

items.activity: Explore Thung Kula Ronghai, photograph the wide rice fields and stop at a Thung Kula jasmine rice learning center
items.note: The fields look best when green (August–October) or near harvest (November–December); in dry season they're a bare brown plain

items.activity: Lunch on Thung Kula jasmine rice with local Isan food in Suwannaphum district
items.note: Thung Kula jasmine rice is famous for its fragrance and soft texture — try it with larb, koi and som tam

items.activity: Pick up some Thung Kula jasmine rice as a souvenir before heading back
items.note: Thung Kula jasmine rice is a GI product and an easy souvenir to take home, sold at shops around the district

items.activity: Set off home; if flying back, leave time to reach Roi Et airport
items.note: Driving back to Bangkok takes 7–8 hours, so an afternoon start means a late arrival — consider an overnight stop on the way

blocks.title: A tip about the seasons
blocks.html: Thung Kula Ronghai doesn't look the same all year. To see green rice fields, come in the rainy season into early cool season (August–December). In dry season (March–May) the plain is bare, dry and very hot — you can still visit, but the scene looks very different from what you see in reviews. · If you come at harvest time, some areas hold merit festivals and new-rice markets worth a stop.

blocks.text: Rough budget per person (3 days 2 nights)

items: 2 nights' lodging — a hotel in Roi Et city runs about 1,000–2,500 THB per night depending on standard (split it if you're traveling with others)
Food — local dishes at 50–150 THB a plate, around 900–1,300 THB for the whole trip
Entry fees — Ho Wood 101 around 50 THB · Bueng Phlan Chai, Prang Ku, the great pagoda and Thung Kula are free (the pagoda may have a donation box)
Fuel — driving around the province across all three days (city–Selaphum–Nong Phok–Suwannaphum) is about 800–1,200 THB per car
Total estimate — traveling as a couple or small group, roughly 2,500–4,000 THB per person (not including getting to Roi Et or the car rental)

blocks.text: Can you visit Roi Et without your own car?

blocks.html: Within Roi Et city you can get around without a car: Bueng Phlan Chai, Ho Wood 101 and Wat Burapha Phiram are close together, and a Grab or motorbike taxi makes it easy. But the out-of-town spots — Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol, Bueng Kluea and Thung Kula Ronghai — are far away and barely served by public transport, so you really need your own vehicle. The options are renting a car to drive yourself (available in town and at the airport) or chartering a van with a driver by the day. If you'd rather not drive, hiring a vehicle day by day works out well and means you don't have to worry about the roads.

faq.q: Where should you stay for 3 days 2 nights in Roi Et?
faq.a: Stay in Roi Et city both nights, because the sights are scattered in different directions and there's no convenient out-of-town lodging hub. Staying in town makes it easy to walk to dinner, head up Ho Wood 101 and visit the Great Buddha, then use the city as a base to drive out to Bueng Kluea and the great pagoda on day two and Thung Kula on day three.

faq.q: How much is entry to Ho Wood 101 and what are the hours?
faq.a: Entry to Ho Wood 101 is around 50 THB, with discounts for students and seniors. Tickets are sold on the 2nd floor roughly 10:00–18:00. The tower is 35 storeys with a 360-degree view over Roi Et city, plus a glass-floor skywalk and a zipline (run in set sessions, roughly 09:30–17:30). Check the zipline schedule on the day.

faq.q: Is Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol far from the city?
faq.a: It's at Wat Pha Nam Thip Thep Prasit Wanaram in Nong Phok district, about 80 km from Roi Et city, around 1.5 hours' drive. The pagoda is 101 m wide, long and tall, set on a green hilltop. Allow time to walk through the interior and dress modestly.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Thung Kula Ronghai?
faq.a: Thung Kula looks best from when the rice is green to near harvest, around August to December, when the plains turn lush green or golden. In dry season (March–May) the fields are bare and dry and the weather is very hot. Thung Kula grows the best jasmine rice in Thailand, so don't forget to buy some Thung Kula jasmine rice as a souvenir.

faq.q: Where is Bueng Kluea and why is it called the sea of Isan?
faq.a: Bueng Kluea is in Selaphum district, a wide freshwater lake with a sandy beach and lakeside restaurants, which is why people jokingly call it the sea of Isan. You can swim, paddle a boat or sit and eat by the water. It's in the same direction as Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol, so you can do both in one day.
